category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Search based on access permissions
prompt: In a shared RAG search system, different departments can access different documents even when they ask the same question. You need to reliably exclude other departments' confidential documents from both model input and the evidence supporting answers.

choices.text: Filter documents at retrieval time using the authenticated user's permissions
choices.explanation: Unauthorized documents can be excluded before they enter the generation context.

choices.text: Filter only the citations by permission after generation
choices.explanation: Removing citations does not prevent leakage from the generation context or answer text.

choices.text: Only instruct the model, “Do not reveal confidential information”
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee authorization for documents included in search results.

choices.text: Reduce the maximum number of tokens in the answer
choices.explanation: This changes output length, but not which documents can be accessed.

learning.reason: Unauthorized documents can be excluded before they enter the generation context.
learning.concept: Apply application-level authorization to search and retrieval, and keep model behavior separate from permission boundaries.

category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Structured tool calling
prompt: A reasoning model outputs the name of an order lookup tool and JSON arguments. Given the possibility of adversarial input or generation errors, prevent it from looking up orders the caller does not own, and reject invalid types before execution.

choices.text: Explain the format and permissions in the system prompt, then use the result as is
choices.explanation: This does not validate before execution that the model followed the instructions.

choices.text: Only enable structured output from the model
choices.explanation: Constraining the format does not verify ownership of the target order.

choices.text: Let a document retrieved from a third party decide whether execution is allowed
choices.explanation: This uses untrusted content to make the application's authorization decision.

choices.text: Validate the tool-argument schema and authorization in the application before execution
choices.explanation: The application can enforce configured constraints and authorization on generated arguments.

learning.reason: The application can enforce configured constraints and authorization on generated arguments.
learning.concept: The model proposes tool calls; authentication, authorization, and validation are the application's responsibility.

category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Measuring evidence-aligned answers
prompt: In retrieval evaluation, nearly all of the correct supporting document IDs are returned. However, the answer generator sometimes adds rules that do not exist. Which metric can be used to compare generation-stage changes independently?

choices.text: The proportion of answer claims supported by the retrieved documents
choices.explanation: This directly evaluates whether generation remains grounded after retrieval succeeds.

choices.text: Retrieval Recall@K
choices.explanation: This measures whether relevant documents were retrieved; it does not determine whether generated claims are supported.

choices.text: The number of documents in the search index
choices.explanation: The document count does not show whether answers correspond to their evidence.

choices.text: Average inference request latency
choices.explanation: Lower latency does not show alignment with evidence.

learning.reason: This directly evaluates whether generation remains grounded after retrieval succeeds.
learning.concept: Measure retrieval Recall and ranking separately from generation grounding and answer quality.

category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Reusing a static prefix
prompt: With a supported model, the same long policy appears at the start of each request, while only the question at the end changes. You want to retain the full policy but reduce repeated processing of the shared portion during inference calls made within a short period.

choices.text: Only lower maxTokens for the output
choices.explanation: Restricting output generation does not reuse the shared portion of the input.

choices.text: Store the entire answer under the same cache key regardless of the question
choices.explanation: This would return the same output for different questions.

choices.text: Use Bedrock prompt caching for the shared prefix
choices.explanation: It can reuse the common input portion and, under supported conditions, reduce input costs or latency.

choices.text: Set the temperature to 0
choices.explanation: This may reduce output variability, but it does not reduce repeated input processing.

learning.reason: It can reuse the common input portion and, under supported conditions, reduce input costs or latency.
learning.concept: Check model support, minimum token requirements, and cache-retention conditions, and place the shared content at the start.

title: Guardrails and authorization
prompt: Of two applications, only one should be able to invoke a specific Bedrock model. Both applications' permissions must address prohibited topics for customers, and the administrator needs to control invocation permission and input/output content separately.

choices.text: Replace IAM with only Guardrails for prohibited topics
choices.explanation: Content evaluation does not grant or restrict permissions for the requesting principal.

choices.text: Use Guardrails for content and IAM for invocation permissions
choices.explanation: This enforces generated-content controls and API access controls separately.

choices.text: Use only IAM roles to control prohibited topics
choices.explanation: IAM determines whether inference can be invoked; it does not evaluate generated text.

choices.text: Only use separate VPC endpoints
choices.explanation: This controls network boundaries; it does not classify input or output content.

learning.reason: This enforces generated-content controls and API access controls separately.
learning.concept: Combine output-policy settings with least-privilege permissions for caller roles and models.

category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Compare quality when making changes
prompt: A new model and a new system prompt have been proposed separately. The requirement is to compare the quality and cost differences caused by each change reproducibly before production, and to exclude any version whose faithfulness to its sources has worsened.

choices.text: Pin the versions and measure each candidate using an evaluation dataset
choices.explanation: The differences can be compared using the same inputs and metrics.

choices.text: Have an operator try just one different input for each candidate
choices.explanation: Input differences cannot be distinguished from model differences.

choices.text: Increase the maximum token count for all candidates and then skip the comparison
choices.explanation: This does not measure actual cost or quality.

choices.text: Evaluate each candidate with an operator’s preferred questions and compare only average response time
choices.explanation: Inputs and quality metrics are not aligned, so the comparison is not fair.

learning.reason: The differences can be compared using the same inputs and metrics.
learning.concept: Measure quality, latency, and token cost on the same cases so the effects of a change can be reproduced.

category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Separate retrieval and generation failures
prompt: You have an evaluation set whose supporting documents for each query are identified by ID. You want to distinguish whether a new model is wrong because retrieval missed the evidence or because generation made an error, then decide what to fix. Which two metrics should you measure?

choices.text: The average number of tokens in generated answers
choices.explanation: This can help estimate cost, but it cannot identify the cause.

choices.text: The proportion of cases in which an expected document ID appears in the top K retrieved results
choices.explanation: This measures whether the retrieval stage found the necessary evidence.

choices.text: For cases where the supporting documents were provided, the proportion of answer claims supported by the evidence
choices.explanation: This isolates generation quality when retrieval has succeeded.

choices.text: Only the user rating that combines both stages
choices.explanation: It shows changes in overall quality, but cannot separate the causes.

choices.text: The status codes of retrieval requests
choices.explanation: Technical success does not show whether the evidence was found.

learning.reason: This measures whether the retrieval stage found the necessary evidence. It isolates generation quality when retrieval has succeeded.
learning.concept: Retrieval evaluation and faithfulness to evidence identify different RAG failure modes.

category: RAG、エージェント、生成AIアプリの運用
title: Retrying a tool with side effects
prompt: An agent calls a purchase confirmation tool. After approval, a timeout may leave it unclear whether the order was confirmed. How should you prevent duplicate purchases on retries and prevent approval from being reused?

choices.text: Bind approval to the user and normalized operation details, and reuse the operation ID as the idempotency key at the payment destination
choices.explanation: Authorization for the operation and uniqueness across multiple submissions can be checked separately.

choices.text: Write “do not make duplicate purchases” in the prompt and accept every request
choices.explanation: Model output alone cannot control external side effects.

choices.text: Share approval as long as requests are in the same model session
choices.explanation: The order details can change within the same session.

choices.text: Generate a new operation ID for each retry
choices.explanation: Each retry may be accepted as a separate operation.

learning.reason: Authorization for the operation and uniqueness across multiple submissions can be checked separately.
learning.concept: Enforce authorization and side-effect controls outside the model, and store the operation ID and result.

title: Too many retrieved results for the model
prompt: In a RAG evaluation, the correct evidence is always retrieved, but the top 20 results strain the input limit and evidence at the end is truncated. Keep the most relevant chunks from the existing candidates without rebuilding the embeddings.

choices.text: Raise the output token limit
choices.explanation: This does not select chunks on the input side.

choices.text: Rerank the retrieved candidates and place the top chunks in the context within the token budget
choices.explanation: This controls relevance and the actual amount passed in without changing the retrieved set.

choices.text: Increase the number of retrieved results to 100
choices.explanation: This makes the input overflow worse.

choices.text: Only lower the generation model’s temperature
choices.explanation: This cannot restore evidence that was not passed in.

learning.reason: This controls relevance and the actual amount passed in without changing the retrieved set.
learning.concept: Measure retrieved evidence separately from the evidence actually passed to inference.

title: Controlling the Ingestion of Model-Generated Data
prompt: A generated result will be stored as a contract record. Even if the JSON is valid, a negative amount or an unknown currency should not be saved and should instead be flagged for investigation.

choices.text: Save the result, then inspect it for errors monthly.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent invalid records from entering the system.

choices.text: Set the sampling temperature to 0.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee that invalid values will not be generated.

choices.text: Save the result as soon as it can be parsed as JSON.
choices.explanation: Semantically invalid values can still pass.

choices.text: Use structured output, then validate the schema and business constraints in the application and quarantine any failures.
choices.explanation: In addition to format guarantees, business logic can enforce semantic constraints.

learning.reason: In addition to format guarantees, business logic can enforce semantic constraints.
learning.concept: Separate structural guarantees during generation from input validation in the system, and place the trust boundary outside the model.
